questions.q: What is the default print behavior in Excel if no print area is defined?
questions.a: By default, Excel prints all data on the current worksheet (all cells with content). A wrong answer like "only the selected cells" or "only the visible screen area" reveals the student confuses print area with selection printing or screen capture, missing that Excel's default is the entire used range of the active sheet.

questions.q: A student sets a print area as A1:D20, then later adds data in column E. They print and column E is missing. Why did this happen, and how to fix it?
questions.a: The print area is static — it does not auto-expand. The fix is to either redefine the print area to include column E (A1:E20) or use a dynamic named range with a table (Ctrl+T) which auto-expands. A wrong answer like "Excel updates print area automatically" shows misunderstanding of print area as a fixed reference, not a live range.

questions.q: You have a wide dataset (columns A to Z) that must fit on one landscape page. Which Page Setup scaling option ensures all columns print on one page width-wise without manually adjusting column widths?
questions.a: In Page Setup → Scaling, select "Fit to: 1 page(s) wide by 99 pages tall" (or a large number for height). This forces horizontal compression to one page while allowing vertical flow. A wrong answer like "Adjust to 75%" shows the student doesn't know the "Fit to" feature, which is the standard way to handle wide reports in board exams.

questions.q: Compare printing a non-contiguous range (e.g., A1:C10 and E1:G10) vs. printing the whole worksheet. How does Excel handle page breaks in each case?
questions.a: Non-contiguous ranges print on separate pages (each selection = new page). Whole worksheet prints continuously with automatic page breaks. A wrong answer like "they print side-by-side on one page" shows confusion — Excel never merges non-adjacent ranges horizontally; each Print Area selection starts a new page.

questions.q: A report prints with "#####" in a date column even though the cell width looks fine on screen. The student widens the column, but the print preview still shows "#####". What is the likely cause and fix?
questions.a: The column width in Page Layout view or Print Preview differs from Normal view due to margins/scaling. Fix: adjust column width in Page Layout view (View → Page Layout) or use "AutoFit Column Width" in Page Layout. A wrong answer like "it's a formula error" shows confusion between display truncation (#####) and actual errors (#VALUE!, #REF!).

questions.q: Design a print setup for a 12-month cash flow statement (columns A:M, rows 1:50) that must: (a) fit on one A4 page, (b) repeat row 1 (headers) on every page if it spills, (c) show "Confidential - Page X of Y" in footer. List the exact steps in order.
questions.a: (1) Set the print area — Page Layout, then Print Area, then Set Print Area over the whole statement, (2) Fit the page — in the Page Setup dialog choose landscape orientation and scale to one page wide by one page tall, (3) Repeat the header — on the Sheet tab set rows to repeat at the top as the header row, (4) Stamp the footer — under the Header and Footer tab build a custom centred footer with dynamic page numbers of the form Confidential, Page X of Y, (5) Verify — use Print Preview before printing to confirm the layout. A poor answer misses the repeat-rows setting or types literal numbers instead of dynamic page codes, showing incomplete mastery of multi-page report setup.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Output Reports in a spreadsheet refer to the process of configuring, previewing, and printing worksheet data in a structured, formatted layout suitable for professional presentation, including defining print areas, setting headers/footers, adjusting page layout, and generating hard copies or print-to-file outputs for ______.
Fill in the blank: Your ______ asks you to print a "Monthly Sales Summary" for the last quarter — but only the region-wise totals, not the 500-row raw data.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to independently set a print area for a specific data range, configure page orientation and margins, insert dynamic headers/footers with page numbers and date, preview the report in Page Layout view, and print a professional-looking report that fits on a specified number of pages without data truncation.
